learningObjective: Given a W4A16 kernel snippet, identify the correct dequantization sequence: unpack INT4 → convert → scale.
stem: The W4A16 inner-loop pseudo-code above shows the standard 'dequant-in-register' sequence. Which is a correct description of what it does and why it works with FP16 Tensor Cores?

options.text: It unpacks two 4-bit weights per byte (sign-extending each nibble to signed int), converts to FP16, then multiplies by the group's FP16 scale to reconstruct the FP16 weight vector; the resulting FP16 vector is fed to an FP16 Tensor Core matmul. HBM traffic is reduced by ~4× vs FP16 storage while compute stays on standard FP16 Tensor Cores.
It uses INT4 Tensor Cores directly; the `__int2half_rn` cast is a no-op emitted by the compiler and is not executed on hardware.
It applies the scale before conversion to FP16, mixing integer arithmetic with FP16 without any explicit conversion; the final FP16 Tensor Core silently interprets the bit pattern as FP16.
It performs the entire GEMM in INT4 without any conversion; the scale is applied only at the end of the K-loop, once per output element.

explanation: The snippet is the canonical W4A16 dequant-in-register pattern: (1) load packed INT4 bytes from HBM, (2) unpack via nibble sign-extension into signed int, (3) convert to FP16 (`__int2half_rn` is a real conversion instruction), (4) multiply by the group's FP16 scale to reconstruct the FP16 weight, (5) feed to an FP16 Tensor Core matmul. HBM traffic drops by ~4× because packed INT4 is stored, but compute uses standard FP16 Tensor Cores (no INT4 Tensor Core is required). Option B fabricates a no-op conversion. Option C misdescribes the numerical composition. Option D wrongly claims INT4 GEMM, which would require INT4 Tensor Core hardware.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: standard W4A16 dequant-in-register + FP16 TC.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: conversion is a real instruction, not a no-op.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: cannot compute with mixed integer / FP16 without explicit conversion.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: INT4 GEMM requires INT4 Tensor Core hardware not used here.

assumptions: Weights packed as two INT4 per byte.
nonImplications: Does not imply the dequant + scale is free — it adds a small number of ops per weight; in bandwidth-bound regimes this is negligible.
Does not imply the same sequence works for asymmetric per-group quantization — an extra zero-point subtraction is needed.

distractorRationales.C: Ignores the need for explicit dtype conversion.
distractorRationales.D: Confuses W4A16 storage with INT4 compute.
